Subject: MAP: Throughput & TTFT gating — evaluation plan and early results

Hi Elena / Simon,

Following our workshop last week, attached is the proposed MAP entry for performance acceptance focused on throughput, TTFT (time-to-first-token), and concurrency gating. This is intentionally narrow so we can get deterministic pass/fail criteria before we start contract signature activities. Key bullets: 

- Staging window: 2027-04-20 08:00 PDT to 2027-04-21 20:00 PDT (see Drive run folder)
- Workload slices: 3 slices (interactive chat, batch summarization, long-context retrieval) with token distributions attached.
- Success criteria (gating):
  - TTFT: 95th percentile <= 150 ms for interactive slice (warm cache);
  - Throughput: sustained 600 tokens/s per GPU for batch summarization (95th percentile over 10m windows);
  - Concurrency: linear scaling up to 150 concurrent sessions with average latency < 300 ms;
  - Error budget: <= 0.5% 5xx per slice.
- Run notes: we will report both warm-cache and cold-start curves; warm-cache baseline will be created with a 30-minute pre-warming pass.
- Artifacts: MAP-staging-config.yaml (attached), run templates in Drive, and the HubSpot playbook link below.

Can you confirm the peak concurrency number Clearline expects and whether the TTFT criterion should use cold-first-token instead of warm? If you have any additional regulatory gating (PII redaction latency constraints), flag them now so we include the check.

Next steps: if you confirm, we'll land the exact traffic mix and kick off a dry run on Apr 20 morning. Final pass/fail report with CSV summary will be delivered by Apr 22 EOD.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP: Throughput & TTFT gating — evaluation plan and early results

Priyom,

Thanks — this is clear and focused, which we appreciate. A few clarifying items before we lock the run shape: 

- Peak concurrency: production target is 120 concurrent live agents during peak hours, but we want a safety factor of 1.25 in the MAP (so test to 150 as you suggested).
- TTFT: for our user experience metric we care most about cold-first-token (customer-facing session start). Can you provide both warm and cold TTFT curves but gate on the cold-first-token 95p <= 200 ms? 
- PII/redaction: we run an inline redaction stage that currently adds ~12–18 ms per token at the middle of the pipeline. Please include a redaction-enabled pass (same workload) and a redaction-disabled pass so we can compare impact.
- Data privacy: confirm that logs for the staging run will be stored in our tenant-only bucket and retained 14 days. Also please include an audit log export for the run.

If you can update the config and confirm the storage/audit flow, we’ll sign off on the staging window.

—Elena
Elena Torres
VP Product, Clearline Health
elena.torres@clearline.health

Elena — quick update from the MAP coordination side and an early snapshot of the dry-run we completed this morning (small traffic). TL;DR: configuration updated as requested (cold/warm TTFT, redaction on/off, stash in tenant bucket). Attached is the CSV with the morning quick-scan; we’ll run full staging at the scheduled window.

Highlights from the dry-run (see attached 20270422-map-results-summary.csv):
- Interactive slice (warm cache): TTFT 95p = 118 ms
- Interactive slice (cold): TTFT 95p = 192 ms (this is with 30s session TTL and single-token prompt)
- Batch summarization sustained throughput: avg 620 tokens/s per GPU during the 15-minute burst window (peak 685 tokens/s)
- Concurrency smoke: we simulated up to 160 concurrent sessions across two GPU pools; median latency remained under 280 ms, tail increased during a garbage-collection spike (we instrumented and flagged for runtime kernel tuning)
- Errors: 0.3% 5xx across all slices (under the 0.5% budget)

Gating recommendation: pass on the initial MAP acceptance criteria with one condition — we include a post-deploy kernel tuning window and an automatic fallback to a smaller-context model if tail latency exceeds 350 ms during business hours. This is already in the rollout policy in the Console.

Next steps (for sign-off):
1) Clearline confirms acceptance of the post-deploy tuning window and fallback policy.
2) Redwood and Clearline run the full staging window Apr 20–21 and produce final pass/fail artifacts by Apr 22 EOD.
3) If pass, we move to a canary on prod traffic with a 48-hour observation window and an agreed rollback SLA.

Thanks — attaching the CSV and the updated MAP-staging-config.yaml to this thread.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

- Results: preliminary staging dry-run meets the gating criteria you requested (cold TTFT 95p = 192 ms <= 200 ms; throughput and error budget within thresholds). Full staging results to be posted by Apr 22 EOD.
- Post-deploy tuning & fallback: Clearline acceptance recorded in HubSpot (see deal log) and we will enable the automatic fallback to the smaller-context model if tail > 350 ms after canary.
- Audit/logs: logs will be placed in tenant-only bucket (retention 14 days) and we will provide the audit export as a GCS link in the final report.
- Next milestone: canary rollout on May 2, 2027 09:00 PDT (48h observation). Redwood will provide a final MAP closure document and a short exec summary for procurement.

Action items for Clearline:
